questions.question: 9 men or 8 women can do a job in 19 days. 9 men work for 9 days and leave. The number of women required to complete the remaining work in 8 days is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

9 men or 8 women can complete the job in 19 days.

9 men worked for 9 days and left.

Remaining work needs to be completed by women in 8 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done = Efficiency × Time

Total Work = LCM of efficiencies × Total Time

**Calculation:**

Efficiency of 9 men = Efficiency of 8 women

Efficiency of 1 man = Efficiency of 8 women / 9

Efficiency of 1 woman = Efficiency of 9 men / 8

Total Work = 9 men × 19 days = 8 women × 19 days

Total Work = LCM of efficiencies × 19

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 7 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 56 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe 1 can fill the tank in 7 minutes.

Pipe 2 can empty the completely filled tank in 56 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Net work per minute = Work done by filling pipe - Work done by emptying pipe

Time to fill part of tank = (Capacity of tank × Total time) / Net work per minute

**Calculation:**

Work done by pipe 1 in 1 minute = 1/7

Work done by pipe 2 in 1 minute = -1/56

Net work per minute = (1/7 - 1/56)

⇒ Net work per minute = (8/56 - 1/56)

⇒ Net work per minute = 7/56

⇒ Net work per minute = 1/8

To fill 3/4 of the tank:

Time = (3/4 × Total capacity) / Net work per minute

⇒ Time = (3/4 × 1) / (1/8)

⇒ Time = (3/4) × 8

⇒ Time = 24/4

⇒ Time = 6 minutes

**The time required to fill three-fourth of the tank is 6 minutes.**

questions.question: The average weight of 10 boys is 70 kg. But later, it was found that at two places the weight 54 kg was read as 44 kg and at one place weight 35 kg was read as 40 kg. Find the correct average weight (in kg) of the 10 boys.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of 10 boys = 70 kg

Incorrect readings:

Two places: 54 kg read as 44 kg

One place: 35 kg read as 40 kg

**Formula Used:**

Correct Average Weight = (Total Correct Weight) / (Number of Boys)

**Calculation:**

Total Weight = Average Weight × Number of Boys

⇒ Total Weight = 70 × 10 = 700 kg

Adjustment for two places:

Difference per place = 54 - 44 = 10

Total Difference = 10 × 2 = 20

Adjustment for one place:

Difference = 35 - 40 = -5

Net Adjustment = 20 + (-5) = 15

Correct Total Weight = 700 + 15 = 715 kg

Correct Average Weight = Correct Total Weight / Number of Boys

⇒ Correct Average Weight = 715 / 10 = 71.5 kg

**The correct average weight of the 10 boys is 71.5 kg.**

questions.question: Mohan invests a sum of ₹5,000 and Varun invests a sum of ₹9,000 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, Varun gets ₹480 more interest than Mohan, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mohan's investment = ₹5,000

Varun's investment = ₹9,000

Time = 3 years

Extra interest earned by Varun = ₹480

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

**Calculation:**

Let the rate of interest per annum = R%

Interest earned by Mohan = (5000 × R × 3) / 100

Interest earned by Varun = (9000 × R × 3) / 100

Difference in interest = ₹480

⇒ (9000 × R × 3) / 100 − (5000 × R × 3) / 100 = 480

⇒ (27000R − 15000R) / 100 = 480

⇒ 12000R / 100 = 480

⇒ 120R = 480

⇒ R = 480 / 120

⇒ R = 4

**The rate of interest per annum is 4%.**

questions.question: Chetan gets a 2% increase in his sale amount in the first year and a 20% increase in the second year; with that his present sale is ₹1,76,800. What was his sale (in ₹) two years ago? (Correct to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Present sale amount = ₹1,76,800

First year increase = 2% (or 0.02)

Second year increase = 20% (or 0.20)

**Formula Used:**

Previous Sale Amount = Present Sale Amount / (1 + First Year Increase) × (1 + Second Year Increase)

**Calculation:**

Let the sale amount 2 years ago be X.

Present Sale = X × (1 + 0.02) × (1 + 0.20)

⇒ 1,76,800 = X × 1.02 × 1.20

⇒ 1,76,800 = X × 1.224

⇒ X = 1,76,800 / 1.224

⇒ X = 1,44,444.44

**The sale amount 2 years ago was ₹1,44,444.44.**

questions.question: Walking at (2)/(3) of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 28 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his destination is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Abhijeet walks at 2/3 of his normal speed and is 28 minutes late.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Difference in time = Normal time - Late time

**Calculations:**

Let normal time be t minutes.

Distance = Speed × Time = S × t

When walking at 2/3 of his normal speed, the new speed becomes 2/3 × S.

The time taken to cover the same distance at this speed is:

New time = (S × t) ÷ (2/3 × S) = (3 × t) ÷ 2

So, the difference in time is:

Difference = New time - Normal time = (3 × t) ÷ 2 - t

Given, the difference in time is 28 minutes:

(3t ÷ 2) - t = 
28

⇒ t ÷ 2 = 28

⇒ t = 56

**∴ The usual time taken by Abhijeet is 56 minutes.**

questions.question: A dealer marks his goods 65% above the cost price and allows a discount of 8% on the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price (C.P.) = 100 (Assume for simplicity).

Marked price (M.P.) = C.P. + 65% of C.P. = 100 + 65% of 100 = 100 + 65 = 165.

Discount = 8% of M.P. = 8% of 165 = 0.08 × 165 = 13.2.

Selling price (S.P.) = M.P. - Discount = 165 - 13.2 = 151.8.

**Formula Used:**

Profit percentage = ((S.P. - C.P.) / C.P.) × 100.

**Calculation:**

Profit = S.P. - C.P. = 151.8 - 100 = 51.8.

Profit percentage = (Profit / C.P.) × 100.

Profit percentage = (51.8 / 100) × 100.

⇒ Profit percentage = 51.8%.

**The dealer's gain percentage is 51.8%, which is Option 2.**

questions.question: The average weight of 14 boys in a class is 40.25 kg and that of the remaining 4 boys is 33.5 kg. Find the average weight (in kg, rounded off to two decimal place) of all the boys in the class.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of 14 boys = 40.25 kg

Average weight of 4 boys = 33.5 kg

**Formula used:**

Average weight of all boys = (Total weight of all boys) ÷ (Total number of boys)

**Calculations:**

Total weight of 14 boys = 14 × 40.25 = 563.5 kg

Total weight of 4 boys = 4 × 33.5 = 134 kg

Total weight of all boys = 563.5 + 134 = 697.5 kg

Total number of boys = 14 + 4 = 18

Average weight of all boys = 697.5 ÷ 18 = 38.75 kg

**∴ The average weight of all the boys in the class is 38.75 kg.**

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 37 and 8?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to determine which number is divisible by both 37 and 8.

Options:

1) 15370

2) 14208

3) 13702

4) 15659

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by both 37 and 8 if it is divisible by their least common multiple (LCM).

LCM of 37 and 8 = 296 (since 37 is prime and 8 = 2³, their LCM is simply 37 × 8).

**Calculation:**

To check divisibility, divide each number by 296:

Option 1: 15370 ÷ 296

⇒ 15370 ÷ 296 = 51.94 (Not an integer, so not divisible)

Option 2: 14208 ÷ 296

⇒ 14208 ÷ 296 = 48 (An integer, so divisible)

Option 3: 13702 ÷ 296

⇒ 13702 ÷ 296 = 46.31 (Not an integer, so not divisible)

Option 4: 15659 ÷ 296

⇒ 15659 ÷ 296 = 52.9 (Not an integer, so not divisible)

**Correct Answer:**

Option 2: 14208

questions.question: Let AB and CD be two parallel lines and PQ be a transversal, such that PQ intersects AB at the point R and CD at the point S. If ∠ARP = 2x°, ∠ARQ = y° and ∠DSP = 4x°, then find the values of x and y, respectively.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB and CD are two parallel lines.

PQ is a transversal intersecting AB at R and CD at S.

∠ARP = 2xº

∠ARQ = yº

∠DSP = 4xº

**Formula Used:**

Using the property of parallel lines, corresponding angles and linear pair property:

1. Corresponding angles are equal.

2. Sum of angles on a straight line is 180º.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fe07c7e7ddf1a18c89eb676ae731ec0a68a53b27c92ab87051d5cc6c1e73d30.png] 

Since AB || CD and PQ is a transversal:

∠DSP corresponds to ∠BRP. Hence:

⇒ ∠BRP = 4x° 

Using the linear pair property at point R:

∠ARP + ∠BRP = 180º

⇒ 2x + 4x = 180

⇒ 6x = 180

⇒ x = 30

Using the linear pair property at point R:

∠ARP + ∠ARQ = 180º

⇒ 2x + y = 180

Substitute x = 30:

⇒ 2(30) + y = 180

⇒ 60 + y = 180

⇒ y = 120

**The values of x and y are 30 and 120 respectively.**

questions.question: The mode and median of a data set is 14.2 and 60, respectively. What is the mean of the data set? (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode = 14.2

Median = 60

**Formula used:**

Empirical formula: Mean − Mode = 3 × (Mean − Median)

**Calculations:**

Mean − 14.2 = 3 × (Mean − 60)

⇒ Mean − 14.2 = 3Mean − 180

⇒ −14.2 + 180 = 3Mean − Mean

⇒ 165.8 = 2Mean

⇒ Mean = 82.9

**∴ The mean of the data set is 82.9**

questions.question: If the quadratic equations 4x² + bx + 3 = 0 and 8x² + 4x + c = 0 have both the roots common, find the values for b and c, respectively.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The quadratic equations are:

4x² + bx + 3 = 0

8x² + 4x + c = 0

Both the quadratic equations have common roots.

**Formula used:**

If two quadratics have common roots, the ratios of the coefficients of their corresponding terms should be equal.

Calculations:

For the equations to have common roots, the following must hold:

(4/8) = (b/4) = (3/c)

From the first ratio:

4/8 = 1/2

⇒ b/4 = 1/2

⇒ b = 2

From the second ratio:

3/c = 1/2

⇒ c = 6

**∴ The values of b and c are 2 and 6, respectively.**

questions.question: If x + y = 14, product of x and y is 45, then the value of x⁴ + y⁴ is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x + y = 14

xy = 45

**Formula used:**

x⁴ + y⁴ = (x² + y²)² - 2(xy)²

**Calculations:**

First, find x² + y² using the identity:

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

Substitute the given values:

14² = x² + y² + 2 × 45

⇒ 196 = x² + y² + 90

⇒ x² + y² = 196 - 90 = 106

Now, substitute x² + y² and xy into the formula for x⁴ + y⁴:

x⁴ + y⁴ = (106)² - 2 × (45)²

⇒ x⁴ + y⁴ = 11236 - 2 × 2025

⇒ x⁴ + y⁴ = 11236 - 4050

⇒ x⁴ + y⁴ = 7186

**∴ The value of x⁴ + y⁴ is 7186.**

questions.question: Rohit marks the price of his article 60% more than its cost price. If he sells the article for ₹18,510 after allowing a discount of 85%, then what will be the cost price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rohit marks the price of his article 60% more than its cost price.

Discount allowed = 85%

Selling Price (SP) = ₹18,510

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 + Markup Percentage / 100)

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (1 - Discount Percentage / 100)

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) = ₹x.

Marked Price (MP) = x × (1 + 60 / 100) = x × 1.6

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 - 85 / 100)

Selling Price (SP) = x × 1.6 × 0.15

Given SP = ₹18,510

⇒ 18,510 = x × 1.6 × 0.15

⇒ 18,510 = x × 0.24

⇒ x = 18,510 / 0.24

⇒ x = 77,125

**The cost price of the article is ₹77,125.**

questions.question: The length of a rectangular park is 27 m more than its breadth. Its area is 2268 m². Its breadth (in m) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the breadth of the rectangular park be x meters.

Length of the rectangular park = x + 27 meters.

Area of the rectangular park = 2268 m².

**Formula used:**

Area = Length × Breadth

**Calculations:**

(x + 27) × x = 2268

⇒ x² + 27x = 2268

⇒ x² + 27x - 2268 = 0

Now, solve this quadratic equation by factorization:

We need two numbers whose product is -2268 and sum is 27. These numbers are 63 and -36.

So, we can factor the equation as:

(x + 63)(x - 36) = 0

Setting each factor equal to zero:

x + 63 = 0 ⇒ x = -63 (This is not a valid solution as the breadth cannot be negative)

x - 36 = 0 ⇒ x = 36

**∴ The breadth of the rectangular park is 36 meters.**
